name: One Million Sense-Tagged Instances
description: Supervised word sense disambiguation (WSD) systems are usually the best performing systems when evaluated on standard benchmarks. However, these systems need annotated training data to function properly. While there are some publicly available open source WSD systems, very few large annotated datasets are available to the research community. The two main goals of this paper are to extract and annotate a large number of samples and release them for public use, and also to evaluate this dataset against some word sense disambiguation and induction tasks. We show that the open source IMS WSD system trained on our dataset achieves stateof-the-art results in standard disambiguation tasks and a recent word sense induction task, outperforming several task submissions and strong baselines.
notes: Large supervised WSD dataset anchored to a sense inventory (e.g., WordNet); potential issues with sense granularity, domain bias, and annotation noise; not designed as an LLM benchmark (possible pretraining contamination depending on downstream model corpora).
